- How much does monday CRM cost?

monday CRM cost depends on the plan you choose and your team size. Plans start from 3 users. If you want to sign up more than 40 users, you can request a quote from our sales team to get an exact price.
- Is there an option for a monthly monday CRM price?

You can pay monthly for your account. By choosing the monthly option on our pricing page, you will be able to pay on a monthly basis. However, monthly plans are not discounted — for this reason we recommend the yearly plan for those looking to save.

We understand that each organization has unique needs, requiring specific features to support specific and multiple projects and workflows. All of our pricing, including our other products, is based on 2 variables: the features you’d like to use, and the number of users. Once you’ve determined the feature plan and users, choose your subscription payment preference: month-to-month or annual plans are available. Payment is made in one upfront installment (if you purchase a plan for one year, you will pay for one year upfront).

monday CRM costs $12 to $28 per seat per month billed yearly, and Zoho CRM costs $14 to $52 per user per month billed annually.

| Plan tier | monday CRM, billed yearly | monday CRM, billed monthly | Zoho CRM, billed annually | Zoho CRM, billed monthly |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Entry | Basic: $12 | Basic: $18 | No paid tier below Standard | No paid tier below Standard |
| First automation tier | Standard: $17 | Standard: $25 | Standard: $14 | Standard: $20 |
| Mid tier | Pro: $28 | Pro: $41 | Professional: $23 | Professional: $35 |
| Upper tier | Ultimate: custom price | Ultimate: custom price | Enterprise: $40 | Enterprise: $50 |
| Top tier | No separate tier | No separate tier | Ultimate: $52 | Ultimate: $65 |

Comparable plans, US-dollar list price per seat (monday CRM) or per user (Zoho CRM) per month, checked October 2026

Sources: monday CRM pricing page (Yearly view at 3, 5 and 10 seats, Monthly view at 10 seats), Zoho CRM pricing page (Annually and Monthly views, US view), checked October 2026.

Zoho’s Free edition ($0 for up to 3 users) does a different job from monday Basic: it sits against monday’s 14-day trial, which the free plan section below compares.

monday CRM’s yearly per-seat price was the same at the 3-, 5- and 10-seat bundles on October 21, 2026. Zoho prints its amounts as “US$”, and both vendors add local taxes on top; monday also says the final price depends on the billing country.

...

Billing terms differ as much as prices. monday charges a yearly plan “in one upfront installment” and gives a prorated refund if you cancel within 30 days of paying. Zoho calls its plans pay-as-you-go, monthly or yearly, with no contract.

...

A 10-rep team pays $2,040 a year on monday CRM Standard and $1,680 on Zoho CRM Standard, and the gap widens when the team needs sequences or falls between seat bundles.

| Scenario | monday CRM | Zoho CRM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 reps, first automation tier | Standard: $17 x 10 seats x 12 months = $2,040 | Standard: $14 x 10 users x 12 months = $1,680 |
| 10 reps who need email sequences | Pro: $28 x 10 seats x 12 months = $3,360 | Standard: $14 x 10 users x 12 months = $1,680 |
| 7 reps, first automation tier | Standard, 10-seat bundle: $17 x 10 seats x 12 months = $2,040 | Standard: $14 x 7 users x 12 months = $1,176 |
| 10 reps, Standard, billed monthly | $25 x 10 seats x 12 months = $3,000 | $20 x 10 users x 12 months = $2,400 |

...

### Seat bundles vs per-user licences

monday CRM sells 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 100 or 200+ seats, so a team between two bundles pays for the larger one. Zoho CRM bills each user and sells team-user licences for staff outside sales.

monday prices its CRM on “the number of users” and lists no viewer or guest seat on its pricing page, so I would budget a paid seat for each delivery or onboarding colleague who works on the CRM’s boards.

The bundle rule also sets a floor. monday says its plans start from 3 users, so a 2-person team pays Basic’s $12 x 3 seats x 12 months = $432 a year. That same pair fits inside Zoho’s Free edition.

title: Zoho Vs. Monday: Which CRM Is Right For Your Business?
text:
### Zoho CRM: tiered pricing for feature-heavy deployments

Zoho offers a low entry price, but you’ll need to upgrade to the Enterprise plan to access the AI and automation features:

| Plan (annual pricing**)** | Main features unlocked |
| --- | --- |
| Standard: $14 per user, per month | Scoring rules, workflows, mass email and custom fields. |
| Professional: $23 per user, per month | SalesSignals (real-time notifications), forecasting and reporting. |
| Enterprise: $40 per user, per month | Zia AI, Blueprints, CommandCenter (customer journey planning), multi-user portals. |
| Ultimate: $52 per user, per month | Advanced business intelligence, higher API limits and a 30-day free trial. |

Zoho has a forever-free plan for up to three users, but it’s fairly limited (no mass email, no forecasting). It also offers a 15-day free trial for all paid plans.

### Monday CRM: flexible entry pricing that scales by seat bundles

Monday uses a seat bucket pricing model, meaning you may have to pay for more seats than you’ll actually use.

You can choose a team size starting at three or five and then increasing by increments of five. If you only need seven seats, for instance, you’ll need to pay for 10, which often makes the real monthly cost higher than the listed price.

Here’s what Monday includes in each tier:

| Plan (annual pricing**)** | Main features unlocked |
| --- | --- |
| Basic: $12 per seat per month | Unlimited customizable CRM pipelines, contacts and mobile app access. |
| Standard: $17 per set per month | Gmail and Outlook sync, merge tags for email and basic automation (250 actions per month). |
| Pro: $28 per seat per month | Sales forecasting, email tracking and high-volume automations (25k actions per month). |
| Enterprise: Custom pricing, call Monday.com to discuss | Reporting and analytics, multi-level permissions and HIPAA compliance. |

Monday offers a 14-day free trial.

title: HubSpot Vs Zoho CRM Vs Monday CRM: 2026 Comparison | Comparison Math
text:
Zoho CRM is incredibly popular among SMBs due to its predictable, transparent pricing. In 2026, its subscription model is divided into highly accessible tiers:

- Free Plan: Free forever for up to 3 users, offering basic lead and contact tracking.
- Standard Plan: $14 per user per month (billed annually). Includes basic pipelines, custom fields, and scoring rules.
- Professional Plan: $23 per user per month (billed annually). Unlocks inventory management, validation rules, and full automated workflows.
- Enterprise Plan: $40 per user per month (billed annually). This is the sweet spot for most growing organizations, unlocking Zoho’s unique Canvas visual layout editor, Blueprint automation builder, and field-level security.
- Ultimate Plan: $52 per user per month (billed annually). Delivers advanced business intelligence, custom database limits, and priority scaling.
- CRM Plus: $57 per user per month (billed annually). A massive bundle containing 9 full Zoho apps, including Desk, Campaigns, Projects, and Analytics.

...

Unlike its rivals, monday CRM does not offer a free tier. It relies on a 14-day free trial, after which users must commit to one of its paid subscription structures. A critical detail of monday’s pricing is its strict 3-seat minimum requirement on all plans. If you are a solo operator, you will still need to purchase a 3-seat block. The 2026 tiers include:

- Basic CRM: $12 per seat per month (billed annually, or $36/month total). Provides basic lead capturing and visual pipelines.
- Standard CRM: $17 per seat per month (billed annually, or $51/month total). Unlocks two-way email synchronization, activity tracking, and up to 250 automation actions per month.
- Pro CRM: $28 per seat per month (billed annually, or $84/month total). The most popular tier, offering sales forecasting, advanced email sequences, private boards, and up to 25,000 automation actions per month.
- Ultimate CRM: Custom enterprise pricing. Delivers multi-level permissions, robust security governance, advanced analytics, and custom developer API access.

title: monday CRM Cost in 2026: Real Pricing & Hidden Costs
text:
Here's the short answer: monday CRM pricing has multiple tiers: Basic is $12, Standard $17 and Pro $28 per seat per month billed annually, or $18, $25 and $41 billed monthly. Each plan starts at three seats, and above five you buy seats in buckets of five. Monday CRM Ultimate, the plan Monday CRM used to call Enterprise, is custom-priced, but in our experience, expect it to be $65 per seat per month sold in minimum blocks of five, with discounts unlocking above 50 seats, paid annually upfront (or paid quarterly only if the total annual subscription is above $20,000 and each quarterly payment is a minimum of $5,000). There's no free plan, only a 14-day trial.

...

## How Much Does monday CRM Cost in 2026?

monday CRM pricing runs on two variables: the plan you choose and the number of seats. A seat is one paid user. Every plan is priced per seat per month, and annual billing is paid upfront for the full year.

monday CRM pricing plans (verified from their website on 23 September 2026)

| Plan | Annual billing (per seat/month) | Monthly billing (per seat/month) | Built for | Key limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | $12 | $18 | Tracking contacts and deals, nothing automated | 1,000 active contacts and deals, 1 dashboard, 5 columns per board, no AI listed |
| Standard | $17 | $25 | Small teams starting to automate | 10,000 contacts and deals, 250 automations a month, email sync and a unified activity timeline, AI credits included |
| Pro | $28 | $41 | Teams running a real sales process | 100,000 contacts and deals, 25,000 automations a month, email sequences, mass email, forecasting, AI credits included |
| Ultimate | Custom | Custom | Regulated or larger teams | Unlimited contacts and dashboards, HIPAA compliance, advanced permissions, white-glove migration, 25,000 API calls a day |

Ultimate is the new name for Enterprise, so any guide quoting "Enterprise" pricing is describing the same plan. Above 40 seats, Monday quotes you on every plan. In our experience, Ultimate usually starts at $65 per seat per month. Treat that as where a budgeting conversation with your CFO should start because it's not an officially listed price. But if you've been shopping around, you'll notice this is still way less than the other "real CRMs" monday CRM is always compared to (ie. HubSpot and Salesforce).

...

monday doesn't sell one seat at a time. Plans start at three seats, then five, then move in buckets of five, so seven reps buy ten seats, and twelve buy fifteen. We priced out what five-seat buckets do to a seven-rep team when we compared monday CRM with HubSpot, and it's the line most buyers don't see right away when they're in procurement mode.
